t: The caves were cut in two phases: a first group of about the 2nd century BCE to 1st century CE, and a second, larger group in the 5th century CE, which Walter Spink dates to the years 460 to 480 and other scholars place over a longer span.

Caves 1, 2, 16 and 17 form the largest surviving body of ancient Indian wall painting, which mostly tells the Jataka tales of the Buddha's past lives; the later caves were paid for by single patrons seeking merit.

The site was known to local people and to pilgrims long before 1819, and its murals have since been damaged by neglect, varnish and cleaning, while many 19th-century copies of them were lost in fires.
dyk: In 1819 a British officer scratched his name and the date over a painting of a bodhisattva in Cave 10; because he stood on a five-foot pile of rubble, the inscription now sits well above the eye level of an adult.
ev: The earliest caves were begun, and the oldest inscription at the site, in Cave 10, is dated by its Brahmi letters to about this time
The Chinese pilgrim Faxian recorded Buddhist pilgrims visiting the site
Work on new caves began in many places at once under Harishena's court, according to Spink
Harishena died, and major excavation soon ceased except at Cave 26
John Smith, guided by a local shepherd boy to Cave 10, brought the caves to the attention of the British
A fire at the Crystal Palace in London destroyed all but four of Robert Gill's 27 copies of the murals
The last Nizam of Hyderabad had Italian restorers work on the paintings and turned the site into a museum
The Ajanta Caves were listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site

f.made: Buddhist monks, patrons and artisans in two phases: the first possibly under the Satavahana dynasty or the Maurya Empire, the second under donors at the court of the Vakataka emperor Harishena (Harisena), including his minister Varahadeva and the sub-king Upendragupta
f.form: 30 caves cut from flood basalt in a 75-metre wall of rock: viharas (monasteries) with square halls and cells, and chaitya-grihas (worship halls) with a stupa in an apse; murals in dry fresco, and rock-cut sculpture
f.where: The northern wall of the U-shaped gorge of the River Waghur on the Deccan Plateau, in Aurangabad district, Maharashtra, India; copies of the paintings are held among others by the Victoria and Albert Museum
f.known: Jataka scenes painted in Caves 1, 2, 16 and 17; the bodhisattvas Padmapani and Vajrapani in Cave 1; the oldest surviving ancient Indian murals in Caves 10 and 11; the stupa-fronted Buddha in Caves 19 and 26; Spink's disputed brief chronology; the tiger-hunting party of 1819
